title: "Introduction to Computational Imaging — Review"

## Basic definitions

::: {.callout-note title="Computational Imaging"}
**Indirect** formation of images from raw measurements via supercomputing algorithms. Tight sensor ↔ algorithm integration.
:::

| | Traditional imagery | Computational Imaging |
|---|---|---|
| **Optical** | Capture the final image | Encode an intermediate representation |
| **Calculation** | Improves recognizable image | **Reconstructed** the image (inverse problem) |
| **Result** | 1 enhanced image | 1 or more final images |

---

## The 3 pillars

- **Mathematics**: optimization, signal processing, ML
- **Physics**: geometric / wave optics / E&M
- **Calculation**: reconstruction algorithms, AI

::: {.callout-tip title="CI Pipeline"}
Real world → **Generalized optics** → Coded representation → **Generalized computation** → Final images
:::

## Optical modeling levels

| Model | Light | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Geometric Optics (Geometric Optics) | Rays | Classic cameras |
| Wave Optics (Wave Optics) | Wave | Microscopy, holography |
| Electromagnetism (E&M) | Full EM field | Nano-imaging, THz |

## Two fundamental steps

1. **Optical Encoding** (Optical Encoding) — new optics, sensors, illumination
2. **Computational Recovery** — reconstruction algorithms

## Medical imaging — Classification

| Method | Porter | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Ultrasound (Ultrasound) | Pressure waves | Backscatter |
| X-ray | Ionizing radiation | Transmission |
| CT/C-arm | Ionizing radiation | Transmission |
| SPECT/PET | Ionizing radiation | Broadcast |
| MRI (MRI) | Nuclear spin precession | Magnetic resonance |

**Pipeline:** 1D/2D multi-signal acquisition → 3D reconstruction (inverse problem)

**Advanced MRI Modalities:**

- **fMRI**: brain activity (BOLD signal)
- **MRA**: blood vessels
- **MRS**: tissue chemical composition
- **CDI**: distribution of electrical currents

| | SKA1-Low | SKA1-Mid |
|---|---|---|
| Site | Murchison, Australia | Karoo, South Africa |
| Antennas | 131,072 dipoles | 197 parables |
| Frequencies | 50–350MHz | 0.35–15.4 GHz |

## Nanoimaging — Key techniques

| Technical | Principle | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| SP-STM | Spin-polarized tunnel current | Atomic |
| nc-AFM | Magnetic exchange force | Atomic |
| MRFM | Mechanical force on nuclear spins | ~1nm |
| NV-NanoMRI | Spin defect in diamond | ~0.1nm |
| ESR-STM | Tunnel current + spin | <0.1nm |
| Coherent X-ray | Coherent X-ray diffraction without lens | 5nm (2D) / 10nm (3D) |

## Computational Photography — Techniques

| Technical | Principle |
|---|---|
| HDR+ | Multi-exposure burst fusion |
| Night Fashion | ~15 images aligned + temporal fusion |
| Coded Aperture | Modifying the PSF to encode depth |
| Super-resolution | Merging multiple low-resolution images |
| Focus stacking | Multiple Focus Merge |

## Deep Optics

::: {.callout-tip title="Principle"}
**end-to-end** co-optimization of the physical layer (lens/mask) and the digital layer (neural network).
:::

| Phase | Action |
|---|---|
| Training | Optimization in simulation, gradient through optics + network |
| Inference | Physical manufacturing of optics + network deployment |

**Interpretations:** optical encoder + electronic decoder **OR** hybrid optical-electronic network

---

## NLOS (Non-Line-Of-Sight) Imaging

::: {.callout-note title="Principle"}
Image a hidden object by exploiting **light bounces** on diffuse surfaces.
:::

**Device :**

- Picosecond laser → point illumination of the wall
- SPAD sensor → single photon detection, time resolved
- Galvanometric mirror → wall scanning

**Pipeline:**

1. Measurement of photon flight time (1st, 2nd, 3rd bounce)
2. Raw data: volume (x', y', t) — not recognizable
3. 3D reconstruction by back-projection or compressed sensing

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap"}
The signal of the 3rd bounce is **10–100× weaker** than the 1st bounce → requires noise-robust algorithms.
:::

---

## MA-XRF (Macro X-ray Fluorescence) — Art

**Principle:** X-ray → electron ejection → photon fluorescence characteristic of the element

**Datacube:** (x, y) spatial × energy 0–40 keV (4096 channels)

**Elements → Pigments:**

| Element | Pigment |
|---|---|
| Pb (lead) | Lead white |
| Hg (mercury) | Vermilion (red) |
| Cu (copper) | Azurite / copper green |
| Fe (iron) | Ochres / reds |
| Ca (calcium) | Gesso (preparation) |
| Zn (zinc) | Zinc white |

---

## Stratigraphy of a painting (from bottom to top)

Canvas → Ground Layer → Underdrawing → Imprimatura → Paint Layers → Varnish/Glazes

## Compressive Imaging (Compressive Imaging / Compressed Sensing)

::: {.callout-note title="Principle"}
Exploit the **parsimony** (sparsity) of natural images to reduce the number of measurements.
:::

**Applications:**

- Single-Pixel Camera
- Compressive hyperspectral imaging
- Compressive light field imaging (Light Field)

---

## Inverse problem — General formulation

$$y = Ax + n$$

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $y$ | Measurements (raw data) |
| $A$ | Measurement operator (system physics) |
| $x$ | Unknown image to be reconstructed |
| $n$ | Noise |

::: {.callout-warning title="Critical Trap"}
The problem is often **ill-posed** → requires **regularization** (a priori on $x$).
:::
